Corollary
[membership criterion for $s_p$]

Source: petersen:page-0388 ↗ def:pet-ch10-tp-decomposition 1. ch10:10.1.7Let $(M,g)$ be a simply connected symmetric space. Then $S\in \mathfrak {so}(T_pM)$ lies in $s_p$ if and only if, for all $X,Y\in T_pM$, \[ -S\circ R_{X,Y}+R_{X,Y}\circ S+R_{S(X),Y}+R_{X,S(Y)}=0. \]
Proof

↗ cor:pet-ch10-so-membership-criterion ↗ thm:pet-ch10-cartan-isometry-extension \sketch For $Z\in \mathrm{iso}_p$ and $S=(\nabla Z)_p$, the identity $\mathcal L_ZR=0$ evaluated at $p$ is

\[ 0=-S(R_{X,Y}V)+R_{X,Y}S(V)+R_{S(X),Y}V+R_{X,S(Y)}V, \]

which proves necessity. Conversely, the asserted relation says that the one-parameter group generated by $S$ preserves $R_p$. By subsection 1.2, these linear maps extend to global isometries fixing $p$. Their infinitesimal generator lies in $\mathrm{iso}_p$ and has derivative $S$.

□
